answer: Clone farms collapse when admission needs a split-site weather bond. The applicant locks 18.9 POA and stations two loggers 41 km apart: one on a west-facing shale scarp, one at a glacier snout gauge. For 11 hours both must report 8-minute packets. Mid-shift the network calls a 25-minute gale window on the scarp (gusts 14-22 m/s); the snout logger must show melt-pulse lag of 70-140 minutes, not identical traces. Matching traces or a reused 36-byte logger ID burns 8.5 POA. If one logger dies after minute 30, 14.1 POA is refunded and the applicant is barred 36 hours.
